posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Setback ended up incapped--by the end, cards were at a premium, and I didn't want to ditch them to wake him up. His incap power (letting Fixer use his power again) was better than what Setback was doing on his feet anyway.

 

Key mid-game was using Charge with Alternating Tiger Claw with Jack Handle, then Fixer's power to get rid of the cohorts.  Lots of birds were out at the time, so all the heroes took some pretty big damage, but it had to be done. Huggin and Munnin are too much to overcome if left out together at all.

 

I used the Mysterious Ceremonies to play cards, mostly (I did draw a few times). It was great to set up Fixer fodder.

 

It came down to an Oblivion at the end. The last Darken the Skies came out, the field was full of birds, but Matriarch was down to 4 HP. Nightmist had the Amulet and spare cards, so she could redirect to Matriarch before the birds all died, if needed. In fact, the only way I could lose was if the Oblivion flip was double ones. Four out of the fifteen cards in the deck were ones, so I felt pretty safe, but I was still nervous, because I know how my luck usually goes.

 

I flipped double twos, so Nightmist redirected, and the Dark Watch was able to stand victorious! (Except for Setback, who slipped and fell over).

 

Fixer=5HP, Setback=0HP, Expatriette=10HP, Nightmist=6HP

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Some general hints for people who are struggling:

remember that you get to choose the order in which you hit things with AoE damage. It's not always crucial, but sometimes (such as using cryo ammo in a SMG), you'll want to micromanage the order to make sure to hit things like poisoners, carrion fields, and the matriarch before killing off any birds. 

Shinobi can be incredibly useful in killing off the cohorts. Just remember that they always go after the lowest, so sometimes it can be really useful to wipe the field, even if it means taking a hit. 

Cryo ammo only works if you do damage with it. So you'll need to aim if you want to punch through both cohorts to the matriarch with a pistol or assault rifle. 

Salvage yard retrieves all equipment. Useful for getting back ammo!

Mitigate removes a token, but if you don't have one, you still get the bonus. Cash Out's healing effect works the same way, as long as you have the cards to discard. 

Ammo doesn't destroy itself until after the power is fully resolved. So you can sacrifice it midstream to prevent damage from the matriarch... just remember to micromanage your damage resolution to get the most out of it first. 

Nightmist works MUCH better in a support role with occasional damage in her Dark Watch incarnation.  Take shameless advantage of your base power to set up heedless lashes to get relics and ongoings out faster!

once mysterious ceremonies comes out, stay focused.  It accelerates the environment deck, but you can pull a LOT of clever tricks by having Setback and Nightmist destroy "Master of the temple" before it can activate... or draw cards for nightmist to scout out mistform for tanking purposes, or set up fixer/setback for damage.

hope this helps!

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
That's why I didn't say "all" =).

Most of the time, I set up a game and press play and see how it goes. If it's good, I use that random seed.

Sometimes I am looking for a few specific things. Like the villain starting with a certain card, or heroes having (or not having) something in their hand. I programmatically create thousands of games to find a seed that generates a game with the conditions I want. The more complicated the conditions, the harder it is to find a random seed, so I try to keep it simple.

Last week's would be an example of that, Baron Blade starting with Hasten Doom, Hasten Doom, and Consider the Price of Victory. Everything else in the game was whatever it was. I still play the game and see if it's OK, because 99% of the setup is still unknown to me.

Of course, that won't stop people from claiming that every little thing that happens is a devious trap and I'm the worst person in the world for it =)

I think it's worth reiterating that nothing that happens in a Weekly One-Shot game is any less likely to happen than any time you press "New Game" with the same team. It is literally exactly the same chance.

Bonus numbers! Out of 50 Weekly One-Shots so far:

  • 10 randomized starts
  • 25 fixed seeds where I just tried the game and went with that
  • 12 fixed seeds where I searched for something
  • 3 fixed seeds from "what number are you thinking of" on the community one-shot survey

posts.name: rjc917
posts.cooked:
Well that was a slog, but I got the mint.  I had things set up for Fixer to take out the Cohorts (and pretty much everything else) on his turn, but then the Matriarch started horrifically screeching a cacophony, killing an Apprentice Poisoner, who got revenge by killing off her giant flock of birds.  And since Odin's ravens hadn't been destroyed yet, my heroes were taking a boosted 4 damage for each bird destroyed.  So after all that, everyone but Nightmist was dead, and she was at 2 hp.

Needless to say, Nightmist immediately turned to mist.  And thus began the long process of healing with Starshield Necklace, performing Mysterious Ceremonies to draw lots of cards, and repeatedly reviving Expatriette.  I knew that if I got Matriarch to be lower than me, I could get Zhu Long to start attacking her, but she was at 50 or so hp when this started, so I had a ways to go.

I finally took her out, taking her from the mid 20s to 0 hp in one round.  I became a Master of Magic on my turn to help get my hp above hers.  Then I used my three Mysterious Ceremonies plays to unleash a Heedless Lash which put the Amulet in play, Mistbound Matriarch's deck so she couldn't cause any trouble, and send everything into Obliveon, including three Shinobi Assassins, which leapt off of my deck to finish off the wounded Matriarch when Setback motivated me to use my power.

I don't like Dark Watch or the Matriarch (unless Tachyon is around), and I really thought I had no chance of winning with the way this started out, but this ended up being one of the most intense games of Sentinels I've ever played.
